narration.text: LK-99 went viral as a room-temperature superconductor.
By mid-August 2023, the consensus was clear: it isn't.
In pure form, it's actually an insulator.
It's a copper-doped lead apatite, made in three steps.
One step heats powders to 725 °C for 24 hours.
A real one would let power lines and magnets waste almost nothing.
That's why the claim spread so fast.
So extraordinary materials need replication, not just hype.
